knife.notes: The camps' plain runner: a raider's hood with a small headlamp on its brow (glass X in a steel housing, its strap round the hood), the rust coat, a short blade in the RIGHT fist (point down, a reverse grip).

bowman.notes: Stands off and looses: a deep hood whose brim shades the brow, a short bow (V stave, F string) held at the ready in the LEFT fist, from hip to shoulder; a hide quiver (T) on the back, its fletching (F) over the right shoulder and its strap (N) across the chest. The right hand is empty.

ram.notes: A big man under a raider's hood, a hand wider and deeper than the others: a plank DOOR (M planks, W rivets; its ledged back from behind) on the LEFT arm, a BEAM (V) in the RIGHT fist, gripped at its foot against the shoulder and rising past the hood.

chief.notes: The camp's own: the RED RAG (R) tied across the hood's brow, its knot and tails behind; a cloak of stitched pale hide (F, T stitches, a ragged hem) over the LEFT shoulder; the long knife (W) hung at the RIGHT hip. Both hands are empty.

chief2.notes: THE NEW CHIEF, told from the old at 1:1: bare-headed (dark hair, the ears showing) under the same RED RAG, a full dark beard along the jaw, a laced hide vest (F) over the coat, and a long SPEAR (V shaft, W head) upright in the RIGHT fist; the same cloak of stitched hide over the LEFT shoulder. No knife.

townshield.notes: The town's recruit: a peaked cap, the leather coat, a ROUND wooden shield (F face, V rim, W boss) on the LEFT arm, a hay fork (V haft, W tines) upright in the RIGHT fist.

kin.notes: The kin who keeps a fallen one's place: a grey shawl (G/g) over the head and the shoulders, a long dress of the town's brown with a sash, the shoes stepping under the hem, a lantern (X glass, x rim, N frame, W cap) held low in the RIGHT fist.

wanderer.notes: A neutral traveller of the valley: a wide-brimmed felt hat with a madder band, a poncho of undyed oat wool (the band again along its hem) over a dun tunic, a walking staff (V) in the RIGHT fist. S wave: the LEFT arm raised out of the poncho, the hand open.
